# MORE ABOUT NOSOCOMIAL PNEUMONIA

# Types of nosocomial pneumonia

Hospital acquired pneumonia (HAP): Development of pneumonia 48 hours or more
after hospital admission.

Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP): Pneumonia occurring 48 hours or more
after endotracheal intubation.

# Criteria for diagnosis of pneumonia

1.  Presence of new or progressive infiltrate <AND>

2.  At least two of the following:

> Fever greater than 38 C (100.4 F)

> Leukocytosis or leukopenia

> Purulent bronchial secretions

# HAP OR VAP suspected:

Gram stain and culture of lower respiratory tract secretions and blood cultures
are important for guiding therapy.

[Re-evaluate Nosocomial pneumonia at 72 hours](nosocomial-pneumonia-re-evaluation-at-72-hours)

# Duration of therapy

Treatment for 7 days is generally sufficient if the initial empiric therapy
covered the pathogen and the patient is clinically responding. Narrow therapy to
treat specific pathogen(s) based on results of culture and susceptibility tests.

Longer duration of therapy is recommended for more resistant organisms (e.g.

Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumanni, and Legionella pneumophila).
